chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Many a man gets into mischief because of being spoken well about.

key_terms.مَفْتُونٍ: Enchanted, deluded, or led into error/mischief

ai.seo_question: What is the danger of flattery according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns that the allure of eloquent praise can deceive even the discerning, leading to spiritual or intellectual downfall. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *taqwa* (God-consciousness) as a shield against the subtle corruption of *madh* (praise) and *majd* (glorification). The insight underscores the psychological vulnerability of the self (*nafs*) to external validation, a theme central to ethical self-purification (*tazkiyah*).

en.sayed-ali-raza: 462. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Many a man gets into mischief because of being spoken well about.
